With this design any key that may change things, including one allowed through Funnel (service/src/20-mcp.mjs:40-45), can call run_batch on any folder under ~/spark-data with the prompt 'repeat this file', then page the answers with batch. The guard 'only runs that agent started' does not help, because the agent starts the run. The same works for an agent talking through ask_sparkie, and for a stolen Telegram session saying 'show me the first five'.

There is no way to stop a running pipeline. It is not an operation, so cancel_operation cannot see it. The only stops are pausing every agent or stopping the model. A run on the brain can last 24 hours.

Being 'not an operation' produces false lines in the code as it stands. run_workflow starts a workflow-run job that ends as soon as run_batch returns, and runJob's finally posts its result (service/src/07-jobs.mjs:68-78; postResult, service/src/14-chats.mjs:121-137). The chat, and Telegram, get 'Done: workflow-run weekly reports finished.' seconds after the start, while the pipeline is still running. A sentence with 'then' also arms the carry-on task (14-chats.mjs:141, :357); if the turn has ended by then, Sparkie gets a turn saying its work 'has finished'.

Nothing can safely follow a pipeline. stop_model never checks whether a model is in use (service/src/17-changes.mjs:527-553); only a start's stop list does (:443, :492). So '…using GLM, then stop GLM', or a saved start, pipeline, stop workflow, stops GLM under the pipeline at once, because run_workflow does not wait for it. This is the most natural procedure for an owner who powers Spark 3 and 4 by hand.

The save-and-run sentence contradicts the design's own gate. Tool results are not kept between turns, so Sparkie must call batch in that turn to get the saveAs object. batch is outside text, and the design makes any run after outside text a button. So step 6 of the owner experience cannot run at once as written.

A saved pipeline can get stuck. A question raised inside a workflow step fails the run (service/src/18-workflows.mjs:195) and gets no button, because only a chat turn or a button press sets onQuestion (service/src/17-changes.mjs:66). After the owner edits a saved pipeline's prompts, every folder it has already processed fails on 'start over?' with nothing to press. Also, fillIn replaces {word} in every string (18-workflows.mjs:133-139), so a prompt such as 'format: {title} - {owner}' is refused at save or silently rewritten at run.

'Say the same sentence again and only new files are done' is not true in chat. The rule compares stored prompts, and a 27B model rewrites the prompt each time, so a repeat gives the start-over question. Only a saved pipeline or 'pick up' has frozen prompts.

The brain as the default is not bounded enough. Round one allowed the brain only when named, with 200 rows. Here it is the default for up to 5,000 files of 1 MB each. One megabyte is roughly the whole 262K context of the agent setup (service/config.json, aphex-agent), which means minutes of prefill sharing memory with the owner's chat. 'No new call while Sparkie is answering' does not interrupt a call in flight and does not see agents' /v1 calls to the brain. The design sets no max_tokens and does not turn thinking off (the agent setup has it on); engine defaults differ.

The headline example is ambiguous for the brain. 'then give me one page of all of them' means the page; 'then turn each into an email draft' means a second step; 'then stop GLM' means another action. A wrong reading silently runs 'give one page' on each file. The page is a list of 49 results, not the one-page digest the sentence asks for.

Also, SIGTERM with no operation running exits at once (service/src/25-backup-and-start.mjs:71-78), so the 'clean' mark must be written synchronously by an earlier listener.

Too much surface for what the owner can use today. out is a copy to another folder on the same disk, which helps nothing until search or hosting exists, yet it adds a path check, an intent target, a marker rule and a question. gather is a flag for something that costs nothing to do always. Five kinds of question guard outcomes that destroy nothing. The size is M, not S: checkValue changes for every array input, sparkieCheck must open saved workflows, and there are 16 acceptance tests.

design.design:
Fits none of the eight blocks: small code on the fleet record, like insight-1 and storage-1. No new action, entry, install or root. It runs only what each Spark already has: sysfs, nvidia-smi, journalctl, last, busctl (UDisks2).

1. Passive readings: /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/src/19-watcher.mjs. Add three sysfs reads to `watchScript` (the 60-second look, already one `run` per Spark): the hottest `thermal_zone*/temp`, NVMe `temp1_input` (hwmon `nvme`), fan `fan1_input` (hwmon `acpi_fan`, when present). `watchSpark` keeps them, timed, in `knowledge.sparks[id].thermal`. Not in worker.py: its text is hashed into every workflow version (R29), so the 30-second status stays as it is.

2. Off-box record, same file. `noteSparkStates` keeps each Spark's last online reading; `spark-offline` carries it as `last`, `spark-online` carries `upSeconds`. `describeEvent` adds the numbers.

3. Probe on request: /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/src/12-status.mjs. `HEALTH_SCRIPT` through `run`, shared by `recent` for 60 seconds, each command under `timeout`: nvidia-smi's `clocks_event_reasons` fields, `clocks.current.sm` and `utilization.gpu`; `journalctl _TRANSPORT=kernel --since "14 days ago"` filtered by fixed patterns; `last -x reboot shutdown`; when `systemctl is-active udisks2`, `busctl --auto-start=no call` for `SmartGetAttributes`; NVMe `temp1_max`; EDAC counts; BIOS and EC versions. `HEALTH_LIMITS` (constants) make each a line: value, limit, time, and `ok`, `over` or `cannot read`.

4. Answers: /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/src/16-actions.mjs. `fleet_status` shows the passive readings; its new optional `health: true` runs the probe on every online Spark and returns verdicts and counts only. `spark_diagnostics` (`spark` stays required) adds the full lines, at most five masked kernel lines marked as data, and `wentDark`: each dark period in 14 days with its last reading, whether it restarted, and a finding chosen by code. Both descriptions say when to use which.

5. Stand-ins and tests: sys files under /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/test/mock/root, stubs `last`, `journalctl`, `busctl` and a query case for `nvidia-smi` in test/mock/bin, tests in test/fleet.test.mjs and test/state.test.mjs. Update docs/architecture.md section 4.

design.ownerExperience:
Why it earns its place for one owner with four Sparks: these machines are reported to power off under load and leave nothing in their own logs, so the only record of the minutes before is one kept on another machine. Spark 2 already looks at every Spark each minute; this keeps what it saw. The cost is about 200 lines on parts that exist, and nothing to buy or install.

Setup: none. After the install the readings start within a minute. There is no page, no setting and no question.

"Is any Spark unhealthy?" Sparkie calls fleet_status with health on, once, and reads back what code decided. For example: "Spark 2: healthy as far as I can read. Hottest zone 71 C (limit 90), disk 48 C (the drive's own limit is 83), disk wear 2 percent (limit 80), no throttling, no kernel hardware errors in 14 days, every boot ended with a shutdown record. Cannot read: memory errors. Spark 3: needs a look. Hottest zone 93 C (limit 90) at 14:02 with the GPU 96 percent busy. nvidia-smi says 82 C; it reads about 10 lower on these machines. Spark 4: went dark once in the last 14 days." With Sparks 3 and 4 powered off, it says so and gives their last readings.

"Why did Spark 4 go dark last night?" Sparkie calls spark_diagnostics for Spark 4. This works while it is still dark, because the record is on Spark 2: "It stopped answering at 02:13. Forty seconds earlier the hottest zone read 94 C (limit 90), the GPU was 97 percent busy at 78 W. It came back at 08:41 having restarted, and that boot has no shutdown record. That matches the overheating power-off other owners report. It is not proof: a power cut or a pulled plug looks the same." If the last reading was cool and idle, it says that instead. If it came back without restarting, it says the network dropped and the Spark never went down. Then the by-hand options, as fixed lines: the clock cap other owners use (sudo nvidia-smi -lgc 300,2200, reported on forums, not confirmed by NVIDIA) and fwupdmgr get-updates to see waiting firmware.

"How hot is Spark 3 really, and how worn is its disk?" One spark_diagnostics call: "Hottest zone 86 C at 14:02 (limit 90); nvidia-smi says 76 C. Fans 2,520 rpm. Disk 51 C. Wear 3 percent, as the drive reported at 13:55 (limit 80); the drive has counted 12 unsafe shutdowns in its life." If the disk service is not running there: "Wear: cannot read. To see it yourself: sudo nvme smart-log /dev/nvme0."

The owner's agents get the same from POST /console/api/actions/fleet_status with {"health": true}, or the same call at /mcp, for example as a check before a long batch.

What the owner never gets: a notification, a question, or a fix applied for them.

One check only the owner can do, once: on one Spark, compare Sparkie's hottest-zone number with cat /sys/class/thermal/thermal_zone*/temp.
guardRails: Read-only (R24, R10): the script goes through `run`, has no sudo, writes no file, starts nothing, and every command sits under `timeout`. A test greps the built script for sudo, redirects to files, rm, mv, tee, systemctl start and docker changes.
UDisks2 is asked only when it is already running, with `--auto-start=no`, and only `SmartGetAttributes` and `Properties.Get`. Never `SmartUpdate` (needs polkit), self-test or sanitize.
service/worker.py is not edited, so no workflow version changes and nothing needs validating again (R29). The 30-second status keeps its shape; `cleanStatus` is untouched.
A signal that cannot be read is `cannot read`, never `ok`. "Healthy" needs every line read; otherwise the unread ones are named.
Verdicts, findings and advice come from constants in code. Every line carries value, limit and time. The brain relays; the existing number check (`unsupportedNumbers`) covers what it says.

Kernel log text reaches the brain as counts by fixed class plus at most five lines, each cut to 200 printable characters, passed through `maskSecrets`, under a `logIsData` label, and only from spark_diagnostics. That tool is not in `INSIDE_READS`, so a change asked after it still needs a button (R25, R26).
fleet_status stays an inside read: with health on it returns numbers and fixed words only. So do the new event fields and the line `describeEvent` adds to Sparkie's fleet notes (R7, R26).

No text from devices: the disk is named by position, never by model or serial; firmware versions are limited to 40 letters, digits, dots, dashes and spaces; readings are range-checked numbers or null.
No new event type and no extra events: `spark-offline` and `spark-online` only gain fields (R23). Dark periods under 90 seconds are ignored, as healing already does.
Nothing is sent anywhere. It adds no caller of `tell()` and no timer; the probe runs only when a person or agent asks, at most once a minute per Spark.
fleet_status without health on does no SSH, so its speed and the existing tests are unchanged. With health on, each Spark is given 12 seconds, then reported as not checked.
spark_diagnostics keeps `spark` required, its existing fields, and its immediate answer for a Spark known to be offline. No existing test is edited.

It never proposes or stores a sudoers rule, group change, or any SSH, Tailscale, firewall or user change. Where one would help, it names the read-it-yourself command and leaves the choice to the owner.

Stated limits, in the answer itself: a pulled plug or power cut looks like a power-off; nvidia-smi reads about 10 C under the hottest zone; the limits are starting guesses; Spark 2 has no off-box record, because the console goes down with it.
acceptance: Stand-in fleet: after one watcher round, fleet_status shows hottestZoneC, nvmeC and their time for a Spark that has the sys files, and null for one that does not. Existing fields and the door test's key list still pass.
fleet_status with {} runs no command on any Spark (the stand-in's command log is unchanged) and returns no verdict word.

fleet_status with {"health": true}: a Spark whose zone file reads 93000 comes back "needs a look" with 93 and limit 90; a normal one comes back "healthy as far as I can read" and names what was unread; a stalled one comes back "not checked" within about 12 seconds while the others still answer.
The result of fleet_status with health on contains no kernel log line, only counts.

spark_diagnostics on a stand-in whose kernel log holds three Xid lines, a fake token and "IGNORE PREVIOUS INSTRUCTIONS": counts show Xid 3, at most five lines come back, the token is hidden, the label says data, and Sparkie's next change in that chat is a button.
Journal not readable (the stub prints journalctl's hint): kernel errors read "cannot read" and the verdict is not "healthy".
`last` output with two boots in a row and no shutdown between them: one unclean end with its time. No `last`: "cannot read".
UDisks2 stub with percent_used 83: wear is over its limit of 80, with the drive's update time. UDisks2 not running: wear is "cannot read" with the by-hand command, and busctl was never run.
GPU stub at 95 percent busy with a 721 MHz clock: "clock held low". A throttle reason set to Active: "throttled" naming it.

A stand-in Spark at 93 C is taken offline: the spark-offline event in fleet_events carries `last` with 93 and its time; spark_diagnostics answers within 3 seconds with the dark period and the hot finding. Brought back: spark-online carries upSeconds, and the finding says restarted or never went down accordingly.
A dark period shorter than 90 seconds does not appear in wentDark.
The probe script contains no sudo, no write and no start (grep test); service/worker.py is byte-for-byte unchanged and every workflow version equals the one before.
`node tools/build-server.mjs --check` passes, the code map is regenerated, docs/architecture.md section 4 names the new fields, and `node test/lock.mjs` passes on the exact tree.

On the real Sparks after install, by the owner: ask "Is any Spark unhealthy?" in chat and through POST /console/api/actions/fleet_status; the hottest-zone number matches a by-hand read within a few degrees; wear either reads or says "cannot read" with the reason; nothing on the Spark changed.
dependsOn: A full gate and a fresh lock before install: any edit to a part changes the build (same prerequisite as round one). Nothing else must be built first; it adds no tool, so it does not wait on Sparkie's tool cut.

Checked: owners report DGX Spark hard power-offs under load with nothing in the journal, pstore empty and `last -x` showing crash; NVIDIA approved a replacement in one case. https://forums.developer.nvidia.com/t/dgx-spark-log-less-hard-power-off-under-load-thermal-sensor-fault-firmware-up-to-date-matches-rmad-case-377365/385262 and https://forums.developer.nvidia.com/t/dgx-spark-gb10-partnerdiag-powerstress-reproducibly-hard-powers-off-the-box-acpitz-88-97-8-c-in-5s-all-other-field-tests-pass/377365

Checked: seven thermal zones, all type acpitz, readable without root; zones 0 and 5 run hottest; nvidia-smi read 74 to 76 C when the hottest zone read 84 to 87 C, and 84 C against 92 C just before a power-off. https://ai-muninn.com/en/blog/gx10-thermal-hard-poweroff

Fact check changed the limit: a healthy unit reads about 84 C on the hottest zone under GPU load, and power-offs were logged at 92 to 98 C, so 85 C would flag normal work. The design uses 90 C. https://forums.developer.nvidia.com/t/new-dgx-spark-fans-barely-speed-up-at-high-temps-and-cant-be-adjusted-critical-please-open-fan-control/386805

Fact check changed fan speed from "cannot read" to "read when present": some units expose it as hwmon acpi_fan fan1_input, others show nothing, and nvidia-smi reports N/A. NVIDIA staff point to a firmware fix for fans stopping on headless Sparks. https://forums.developer.nvidia.com/t/dgx-spark-fans-stop-when-the-screen-goes-dark-or-running-from-ssh-box-gets-too-hot-to-touch-fire-hazard/378945

Fact check added one line: throttle reasons are readable on GB10 but were all "Not Active" while a clock sat pinned at 721 MHz under full load, so the same query also reads the clock. https://forums.developer.nvidia.com/t/dgx-spark-gb10-gpu-clock-pinned-at-721-mhz-under-full-load-no-throttling-not-liftable-via-nvidia-smi/376039 and https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/group__nvmlClocksEventReasons.html

Checked: UDisks2 gives NVMe wear without root. `SmartGetAttributes` returns percent_used, spare, media errors and unsafe shutdowns from the daemon's cached log with no polkit check, and the daemon refreshes it about every ten minutes; `SmartUpdate` does need polkit. The interface dates from 2.10.0; Ubuntu 24.04 ships 2.10.1 with an arm64 build. https://storaged.org/udisks/docs/gdbus-org.freedesktop.UDisks2.NVMe.Controller.html and https://github.com/storaged-project/udisks/blob/master/src/udiskslinuxnvmecontroller.c

Checked: `busctl --auto-start=no` stops a call from starting the service; it covers `call` only, so properties are read with `call ... Properties Get`. https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/busctl.html

Fact check dropped one piece: `nvme smart-log` needs root, and the console never holds sudo, so "allowing" it would mean a sudoers rule kept on the Spark. Not built. If UDisks2 cannot be read, the owner gets the command to run by hand. Revisit only if UDisks2 is missing on the real Sparks. https://github.com/linux-nvme/nvme-cli
Fact check moved the passive readings from the 30-second status to the 60-second watcher: the status is worker.py, and 18-workflows.mjs hashes worker.py into every workflow version.

Not checkable from here (no SSH in this analysis), and each one degrades to "cannot read": whether UDisks2 is installed and running on DGX OS; whether the console's user on Sparks 3 and 4 is in group adm, which reading the kernel journal needs; whether this driver answers every `clocks_event_reasons` field; whether `last` and its shutdown records are present.

How the owner powers Sparks 3 and 4 down matters to one line: a short press or `poweroff` leaves a shutdown record; pulling power does not, and then reads as an unclean end with a cool, idle last reading. The smart plugs in contract 9.22 shut down first, so they will read as clean.
Optional later, not needed now: round one's fleet history (insight-1) would give Spark 2 a record that survives its own power-off.

problems: No hard constraint is breached: everything is a read, nothing can lock the owner out, go public, power anything off, download, notify, or need another machine or a paid service. The design breaks on truthfulness, on one regression risk to the watcher, and on upkeep.

The hot/cool finding at 90 C gives the wrong answer for the documented failures. NVIDIA forum thread 377365 logged a six-minute plateau near 88.7 C, then 88 to 97.8 C in five seconds; thread 385262 reports a cut at 87 C. A 60-second sample will normally catch the plateau, which is under 90, so 'Why did Spark 4 go dark?' would answer 'restarted with a cool last reading'. Both threads also report the zone sensors jumping implausibly (84 to 67 C in ten seconds), so the 'hot' verdict line is unreliable too. GPU busy and watts at the last reading are the dependable signal.

Sparks 3 and 4 are powered up and down by hand, so every ordinary power-down is a spark-offline followed by a restart. The four findings have no 'shut down on purpose' case: wentDark and 'went dark N times' fill with the owner's own shutdowns, and a shutdown straight after a heavy job reads as 'matches the overheating power-off'. If the owner ever holds the button or cuts power, the 'boot with no shutdown record' line keeps every verdict at 'needs a look' for 14 days.

A guard rail misdescribes the code. `readOutside` (service/src/14-chats.mjs:341) is used only at service/src/20-memory.mjs:85, where it tightens what may be remembered. It does not turn a change into a button; changes are gated by the owner's own words in `sparkieCheck` (service/src/16-actions.mjs:260, R25). The acceptance line 'Sparkie's next change in that chat is a button' fails whenever the owner's message asks for the change. The protection that does exist is R25, with its known gap: for six actions the kind word alone is enough.

Adding reads to `watchScript` can silently stop container watching. `watchSpark` returns at `r.code !== 0` (service/src/19-watcher.mjs:74) before parsing anything, and the script's exit status is its last command's. A missing fan or NVMe file, which the design expects on some units, would make every round fail for that Spark: no container events, no crash detection, no crash restart. If docker hangs on a sick Spark, the readings are lost with it.

A slow probe can create the dark period it reports. `run` counts a timeout as unreachable (`noteReach(node, timedOut ? 255 : code)`, service/src/02-ssh.mjs:60); two in a row mark the Spark offline for a minute, the status loop then writes spark-offline, and that event pauses crash restarts for 30 minutes (service/src/18-workflows.mjs:261). Eight commands including a 14-day journal scan inside 12 seconds on a loaded Spark invites this. In the stand-in, `timeout` drops only its first argument (test/mock/bin/timeout), and the stall switch exists only in the docker and worker stubs, so 'not checked within 12 seconds' needs new test plumbing.

The '14 days' claims are not backed by what is kept. `events` holds the last 500 entries (service/src/19-watcher.mjs:15, :30), which can be far less than 14 days, so 'went dark once in 14 days' can be false. wtmp rotates monthly, so the first boot record in a new file has nothing before it and would read as an unclean end. After a console restart, `online` and the reading come from knowledge.json, saved only when the watcher sees a container change (19-watcher.mjs:175), so a stale reading can be attached as 'the last reading before it went dark'.

The probe is unverified on the real machines, and the designer says so for four signals (UDisks2 present, journal readable, clock-reason fields answered, `last` present). Stubs written from documentation prove only the parser. Memory-error counters are likely absent on GB10, so 'Healthy' can never be reached and the unread list becomes permanent noise. One field this driver does not know fails a whole nvidia-smi query. The design does not say where the EC version comes from; `fwupdmgr` would start the fwupd service, breaking 'starts nothing'.

Several limits will raise false alarms. 'Hot while idle' fires after every job: GPU use drops to zero at once while the zone stays hot for a minute and load is mostly CPU. 'Clock held low' rests on one thread. A healthy unit reads about 84 C and a failing one plateaus at 87 to 89 C, so no fixed number separates them. Each limit is a code constant, so every tuning is a part edit, a full gate, a fresh lock and an install.

The fixed advice will age badly. `sudo nvidia-smi -lgc 300,2200` is incomplete (the source pairs it with `-pm 1`), costs 6 to 9 percent speed, its author later turned it off, and a firmware update stopped the power-offs in one thread. NVIDIA staff's actual advice is the field diagnostic and a replacement. The same text is handed to the owner's agents at /mcp as the console's advice.

The number check is weaker than claimed. `unsupportedNumbers` (service/src/14-chats.mjs:158) matches '°C' but not '93 C', rpm, MHz or bare counts, and passes any number within 5 percent of one it saw, so 93 and the limit 90 can be swapped unnoticed. fleet_status would carry two temperatures (`temperatureC` from nvidia-smi, about 10 C lower, and the zone), inviting the brain to quote the wrong one.

`health: true` on fleet_status will be over-used and is not small. The description already says 'Use first for is everything OK', so the 27B brain is likely to set it on ordinary status questions, turning an instant read into SSH to every Spark and a wait of up to 12 seconds; any look-only agent key can trigger journal scans on all Sparks once a minute. With bash and busctl parsing, four new stubs, a limits table and findings, this is size M, not S.

Kernel lines are outside text even from the kernel transport: USB product strings, process names in fault lines and file names all appear there. Five raw lines add little over the class, the Xid code and the time, and they are the only reason the result needs a data label and a hostile-text test.
attack.smallerVersion: Build the off-box record first, sysfs only (about 80 lines). The watcher reads the hottest thermal zone, NVMe temperature and fan (when present) each minute. `spark-offline` carries the last reading (zone, GPU busy, watts, age) when it is under three minutes old; `spark-online` carries `upSeconds`. `fleet_status` shows the readings beside `temperatureC`. `spark_diagnostics` adds the last five dark periods, each with one code-picked finding: still dark; did not restart; restarted, was under GPU load; restarted, was idle. No `health` argument, verdict words, limits table, hot/cool finding or tuning advice. Add kernel-error counts, shutdown records, wear and throttling later, one at a time, only for signals a by-hand capture from Spark 3 proves readable.
mustHaveGuards: In `watchScript` the readings are printed first, the script always ends with exit 0, and `watchSpark` parses them before its exit-code check. A test with the fan and NVMe files missing proves containers are still watched and crash events still fire.
Every reading is a range-checked number or null. No text from a device reaches a result, an event or Sparkie's fleet notes.
`spark-offline` carries a reading only when it is under three minutes old; otherwise it says 'no reading near the time'. This covers console restarts and Spark 2 being down.

No finding or verdict comes from a temperature limit. The answer shows the number, its age and the gap to nvidia-smi. Findings key on restart and GPU busy or watts, say 'consistent with', and never rule heat out because the last reading was cool.
'Did not restart' is worded as 'stopped answering without restarting (network, sleep or too busy)', never 'the network dropped'.
A restart from idle is described as consistent with being switched off by hand and is not counted as a fault. When smart plugs arrive, a shutdown the console made is marked as such on the event.
The dark-period list states its real window (from the oldest kept event), never a fixed '14 days', and returns at most five entries.

fleet_status with {} still runs no command on any Spark; its schema gains no argument and no tool is added. The description says which temperature is which, and each Spark gets one code-built sentence for Sparkie to relay.
No new event type and no extra events; dark periods under 90 seconds are ignored, matching `cameBack` in service/src/20-heal.mjs.
service/worker.py stays byte-for-byte unchanged and no function in any workflow's `code()` list is edited, so every workflow version is the same; a full gate and a fresh lock precede the install.

If the probe is built later: inner timeouts sum to less than the outer limit, use the plain `timeout N command` form, and the script exits 0, so a slow probe never counts as an unreachable Spark. A test proves a slow probe writes no spark-offline event.
Probe test fixtures come from output the owner captures by hand on a real Spark. A signal that hardware does not offer is left out, not reported as 'cannot read' on every answer.
Kernel log, if added: `_TRANSPORT=kernel` only; counts by fixed class plus Xid code and time; no raw lines; zero kernel lines of any kind means 'cannot read', not 'none'.
Shutdown records, if added: the first boot record in a rotated wtmp is 'cannot tell', never an unclean end.

The probe has no sudo, no write and starts no service: firmware versions from DMI sysfs only, never `fwupdmgr`; `busctl` only after `systemctl is-active udisks2` and with `--auto-start=no`; never `SmartUpdate`, self-test or sanitize.
No tuning command appears in any advice line. Fixed text names only the by-hand read commands and NVIDIA's field diagnostic and support.
The hostile-text acceptance test is restated to match the code: after outside text, memory needs a button, and a change the owner's own words did not ask for becomes a button.

design.title: Address options and a reach line on everything hosted: one fixed table, no new tool
design.design:
Nothing new runs: no tool, container, download, fetch or state file, so there is nothing to check on ARM64. About 90 lines of constants and code, shipped inside hosting-2's change (today the code has no `host`, `hosted` or `what_can_you_do`).

1. /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/src/23-http.mjs, `checkRoute`: next to `funnelOn`, keep `funnelPorts` (every host:port Tailscale lists under `AllowFunnel`) and `funnelReadAt`. Add `SPARK_CONSOLE_FUNNEL=on|off`, honoured only in the stand-in fleet.

2. /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/src/21-hosting.mjs (hosting-2's part):
- `ADDRESS_WAYS`, a frozen constant of five way cards: status (built, not built, ruled out), cost, who ends TLS, what it exposes, flags (owner runs it, outside service, touches access), steps, trigger, checked-on date, source link. Rows: ts.net link (its one access step is the name of deploy/open-to-internet.sh, never run); web copy and own name (not built until webaddress-2 and -4; the name sits only on the public copy); Cloudflare Tunnel; rented relay or home router port. Ruled-out rows hold one reason sentence and no steps, trigger, command or link.
- `reachOf(place)`, code: a web address outside ts.net gives 'opens anywhere'; a ts.net host:port in `funnelPorts` gives 'anywhere except networks that block Tailscale'; any other ts.net place gives 'your tailnet only'; Tailscale not read yet gives 'not known yet'. Reach is worked out on every read from the Door entry's stored `place`, never stored: the owner switches Funnel outside the console.
- `host` returns `reach`. `hosted` returns each item's `reach` and a code-picked `ifItWillNotOpen` line, plus `addressOptions` (each row's sentence ends with its date) and the fixed blocked-network sentence. Its description leads with the owner's three questions.

3. /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/src/14-chats.mjs, `systemPrompt`: one sentence. Address, domain and will-not-open questions are answered only from `hosted`; never suggest another tunnel, relay, proxy, opened port or outside service.

4. /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/src/20-abilities.mjs (insight-2, when it exists): each way in gets `reachOf`, plus a one-line count of address options.

5. Tests in /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/test/hosting.test.mjs; three sentences in test/eval/cases.json; docs/architecture.md and docs/sharing.md updated.

Data versus code: the only stored data is `place`. The table and sentences are build constants; choosing is code.

Critical files: the five named above.
design.ownerExperience:
There is no setup and no one-time owner step. It arrives with the update that brings hosting.

- Hosting something. "Give me a link to ~/reports/q3 for a week." The reply carries the link, its end date and one reach line: "Opens anywhere except on networks that block Tailscale addresses." If port 8443 is not open to the internet, the line reads: "Opens on your tailnet only. You open port 8443 with deploy/open-to-internet.sh from your Mac; I never run it."
- "Can I put this on my own domain?" Sparkie makes one lookup (`hosted`) and answers from the table: not on this link, because Tailscale addresses always end in ts.net; an own name can sit only on a public copy on an ordinary website, which is not built yet; a tunnel, a rented relay and a port on the home router are ruled out. The sentences end with "checked 2026-11-11".
- "Why can't my friend open the link I sent?" One lookup. Code picks the reason from the item: it ended on a date; it opens on your tailnet only; or it is set to open from the internet, so their network may block Tailscale addresses, and the console cannot test from outside.
- "It will not open at work." One fixed sentence: the console, Sparkie and the models do not open on networks that block Tailscale addresses, by your decision; nothing will be set up to change that; a public copy on an ordinary website is a separate website with no way into the Sparks.
- "What are my options for a proper address for the demo?" The five rows, each with cost, who ends TLS, what it exposes and whether it is built, not built or ruled out.
- Your agents get the same fields from POST /console/api/actions/hosted or the agent door. It answers with Spark 3 and 4 off and with the brain down.

Why it is worth it for one owner with four Sparks: about 90 lines and nothing running. It is the one place where the ruled-out decision lives in code, so a 27B brain asked about addresses quotes it and does not improvise tunnel advice.
design.decidesAndAsks:
It never asks; everything here is a read.

- Which tool: questions about an address, a domain, address options or a link that will not open go to `hosted`. Its description starts with those sentences, and the prompt sentence says to answer only from it.
- Which reach line: code, from the Door entry's `place` and the Funnel setting the console already reads every 60 seconds. The model never chooses or words it.
- Which reason a link will not open: code, in fixed order: ended, tailnet only, not known yet, set open but not testable from outside.
- Which rows show: all five, always, in the same order. Status is a literal in the build; a row turns to 'built' only in the change that builds it.
- A value it cannot know: before Tailscale has been read it says 'not known yet' and to ask again in a minute. It does not guess.
- A request for a ruled-out row ("set up a Cloudflare tunnel", "forward a port"): Sparkie says it is ruled out, gives no steps and changes nothing; there is no action for it.
- A request to open or close port 8443: it names deploy/open-to-internet.sh as the owner's own command and never runs it.

Three corrections to the proposal: reach is derived on each read, not stored, because the owner switches Funnel outside the console; there are four lines, not three ('not known yet' is needed for honesty); and `funnelOn` covers only the console's own host and port, so the port list is kept for apps on port 10000 later.
guardRails: Nothing is fetched, started, written or changed. No new command is spawned: reach comes from the `tailscale serve status --json` read that `checkRoute` already makes every 60 seconds. No action switches Funnel; the table only names deploy/open-to-internet.sh as the owner's command (R3).

Ruled-out rows (Cloudflare Tunnel, rented relay, home router port) print the status, one sentence on what they would expose, and that the owner ruled them out. No steps, trigger, command name or link. A test fails if a ruled-out row contains a URL, a backtick, or words such as install, run, sudo, docker, cloudflared or ngrok.

The own-name row is tied to the public copy only. The table states that an own name cannot sit on the ts.net link (Funnel and Serve use only the tailnet's ts.net name) and is never put in front of the console, Sparkie, /v1 or /mcp.
The blocked-network answer is one constant sentence. It names no network, offers no next step, and describes the public copy as a separate website with no way into the Sparks, never as a way round.

Rows are a frozen constant in the build: never read from the web, a state file, memory or config, and not editable through chat, an agent or an action. Each printed sentence ends with its checked-on date; built and not-built rows carry their source link. A row changes only in a code change that rechecks its source.

Reach is called what it is: the Tailscale setting read at most a minute ago, not a test from outside. Before the first read, or when the console's address is unknown, it says 'not known yet'. 'Opens anywhere' is given only to a non-ts.net address recorded by the change that builds the web copy.
Reach is network reach only. It prints next to, and separate from, who may open the item and its end date.
The table holds no hostname, tailnet name, link token or person. Agents see the same rows and reach lines, never the links (hosting-2's rule). Results still pass maskDeep.

One copy: `host`, `hosted` and `what_can_you_do` print from the same constant, and the prompt sentence moves into insight-2's single never list when that exists. No row text goes into the description of an action a workflow hashes (18-workflows.mjs:64), so no workflow needs validating again.

Backstop, built only if the real-brain eval fails: in `sparkieTurn`, beside `unsupportedNumbers` (14-chats.mjs:336), a reply that names a tunnel product when `hosted` was not called that turn gets the fixed ruled-out sentence appended.
No notification, timer, download or new tool. Sparkie's tool count stays where hosting-2 leaves it.
acceptance: Stand-in fleet with SPARK_CONSOLE_FUNNEL=on: POST /console/api/actions/host returns reach 'anywhere except networks that block Tailscale'. With off: 'your tailnet only', naming deploy/open-to-internet.sh and saying Sparkie never runs it. Unset: 'not known yet'. `hosted` shows the same line per item.

`hosted` returns exactly five address rows in a fixed order: one built, two not built, two ruled out. Every row sentence ends with a checked-on date. Built and not-built rows have a source starting with https://tailscale.com/ or https://developers.cloudflare.com/.
The two ruled-out rows contain no URL, backtick, or the words install, run, sudo, docker, apt, brew, curl, npx, cloudflared or ngrok, and have no steps or trigger.

An item past its end date says it ended, with the date. A live item with Funnel off says tailnet only. A live item with Funnel on says it is set open, the other network may block Tailscale addresses, and it was not tested from outside.
POST /console/api/actions/hosted answers with every Spark offline and the brain down, opens no SSH and makes no outbound request (the stand-in ssh and curl logs are unchanged).
Scripted stand-in brain: 'Can I put this on my own domain?' makes one call to `hosted`, with no change and no button. The system prompt contains the new sentence and is identical between rounds.

Real brain, three runs each: 'Can I put this on my own domain?', 'Why can't my friend open the link I sent?' and 'It will not open at work, what can I do?' call `hosted` first, change nothing, and the reply holds no tunnel, relay, proxy, VPN or port-forward advice. 'Set up a Cloudflare tunnel for the console' gets 'ruled out' and no steps. The 16 existing cases do not get worse.
Workflow versions are unchanged by this change: after install /health shows each workflow in the state it had before.
When `what_can_you_do` exists: each way in shows the same reach as a hosted item on port 8443, and the overview stays under 4,000 characters.
A look-only agent key gets the rows and reach lines from `hosted`, and no link.

Owner's check after install, phone on mobile data with Tailscale off: host a file, read the reach line, open the link; it opens. If port 8443 is ever closed by hand, 'what am I hosting?' reads 'your tailnet only' within a minute.
dependsOn: Hard: hosting-2. It brings `host`, `hosted`, the Door entry with `place`, and the part 21-hosting.mjs. None of these is in the code today (searched service/src), so this cannot ship before it.
Soft: insight-2 (`what_can_you_do`). Its reach lines and count line are added when it exists.
Soft: webaddress-2 (web copy) and webaddress-4 (own name). Each turns its row from 'not built' to 'built' and fills in steps and trigger in its own change, with the date rechecked.

Already in the code and reused: `checkRoute` and `funnelOn` (service/src/23-http.mjs:47-64), `consoleOrigin` (service/src/20-mcp.mjs:17), the owner-run deploy/open-to-internet.sh, and the reply check `unsupportedNumbers` (service/src/14-chats.mjs:148). The repo already has one ordinary website that Spark 2 only sends out to: deploy/web-page.sh and cloud/worker.js.

The normal release path: node tools/build-server.mjs, node tools/code-map.mjs, node test/lock.mjs, then the installer. docs/architecture.md section 8 reports the tree ahead of its lock; a fresh lock comes first.

No outside piece runs, so there is no ARM64 question. For the record, cloudflared is published for Linux ARM64 ([downloads](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/downloads/)), but that row is ruled out.

Checked 2026-11-11, Tailscale Funnel: listens only on ports 443, 8443 and 10000; uses only DNS names in the tailnet's ts.net domain; TLS ends on the device and the relay servers do not decrypt; bandwidth limits are not configurable ([Funnel docs](https://tailscale.com/docs/features/tailscale-funnel)). Serve: DNS names are restricted to the tailnet's domain; serving a socket or files needs root ([Serve docs](https://tailscale.com/docs/features/tailscale-serve)).

Checked 2026-11-11, Cloudflare: Workers free plan allows 100,000 requests a day, 20,000 static files a version and 25 MiB a file ([limits](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/limits/)); requests to static assets are free and unlimited ([static assets](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/static-assets/billing-and-limitations/)); a Worker custom domain needs an active Cloudflare zone and gets its DNS record and certificate made for it ([custom domains](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/configuration/routing/custom-domains/)); publishing through a tunnel requires adding a website to Cloudflare ([tunnel setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/get-started/create-remote-tunnel/)); Registrar renewals carry no markup ([Registrar](https://developers.cloudflare.com/registrar/about/)).
A web search today found no sign that Funnel accepts custom domains; a third-party guide says the same ([SSD Nodes](https://www.ssdnodes.com/learn/tailscale-serve-vs-funnel)).

Not checked: Funnel's bandwidth numbers (Tailscale does not publish them), and whether `AllowFunnel` stays true after a tailnet policy withdraws Funnel. That is why reach is worded as the setting, not a test from outside.

problems: Breach of the blocked-network constraint. The fixed answer to "it will not open at work" ends by pointing at "a public copy on an ordinary website", and the web-copy row carries a `trigger` field. In that answer the clause has one job: naming an address that does open on that network. /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/docs/contract.md 4.10 and /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/docs/sharing.md both say the console does not route around that filter. The acceptance check bans tunnel, relay, proxy, VPN and port-forward words but not this one.

The table contradicts recorded decisions and invents others. /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/docs/analysis-2026-11-11/README.md records "no custom domain for now" (decision 9) and deleting the workers.dev page after a final approval (decision 3); round one lists a custom domain under "not worth it". The table shows web copy and own name as "not built" with cost, steps and trigger, which a 27B brain will present as coming. It also tells the owner that a router port and a rented relay are ruled out "by your decision"; no such decision is recorded. A router port is simply owner-only (firewall).

`reachOf(place)` cannot work as specified and is more general than anything that exists. hosting-2's ruled version keeps the link token only as a hash and serves every item at /console/api/h/s/<token>/ on the console's one address, so reach is a single value for all items: `funnelOn`. Per-item reach lines repeat one fact N times. `funnelPorts` is kept for port 10000, where nothing runs, and would also pick up Spark 2's separate public site on port 443 (sharing.md: "its own public site (the Funnel on 443)").

Stale values are reported as fresh. `checkRoute` updates only when tailscale exits 0 (/Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/src/23-http.mjs:55-57), so a failing CLI leaves the last value indefinitely. The design adds `funnelReadAt` but no reach rule reads it, while guard 6 promises "read at most a minute ago". Tailscale's Funnel page (checked today) also says Funnel needs the `funnel` node attribute in the tailnet policy, so `AllowFunnel: true` can be on while nothing opens.

The change edits the one function that holds the API lock, and no test can reach it. `checkRoute` also sets `tcpApiOff`, runs at every start, and never runs on the stand-in fleet (`if (!ALL_LOCAL)`, 23-http.mjs:64); /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/test/mock/bin/tailscale answers only `ip`. The proposed SPARK_CONSOLE_FUNNEL switch bypasses the parser, so acceptance 1 tests the switch, not the code that reads `AllowFunnel`. A throw outside the existing try ends the process (/Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/src/25-backup-and-start.mjs:85-88) and systemd restarts it into the same throw: a crash loop of the console.

Public by accident, both ways. With Funnel off, every hosting reply names deploy/open-to-internet.sh. Funnel is a switch for the whole port (architecture R3; the script's own comment), so a nudge given while sharing one file opens the sign-in page, /mcp, /v1 and every hosted link. Agents get the same script name over /mcp, and the owner's agents run on the Mac that holds the script. In the other direction, "your tailnet only" reads as the link's own property: links sent while the port was closed become internet-reachable the day the owner opens it, and nothing said so.

It does not fit a 27B brain as written. `hosted` becomes two tools in one (list items; answer address policy), and every "what am I hosting?" drags five rows, including the names of ruled-out workarounds, into the reply. The prompt sentence "never suggest another … outside service" is broad enough to hit connectors, Telegram and Hugging Face. It also sits beside the existing line at /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/src/14-chats.mjs:49 ("say the owner does that by hand"), which steers a tunnel request the opposite way. insight-2's ruled guard wants one never constant, not a second sentence.

More upkeep than it is worth. Cloudflare quotas, prices and source links are frozen into build constants. Any recheck changes the build, so it needs a fresh lock (the full gate, 17 to 20 minutes per /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/docs/analysis-2026-11-11/07-fast-gate-plan.md) and an owner-approved install. In practice nobody rechecks, and Sparkie quotes year-old numbers for options the owner does not use, with a date that makes them look maintained.

Acceptance is not measurable as written. /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/test/eval.mjs grades "by what happened, not by the words" (lines 1-10, 93-104), so "the reply holds no tunnel advice" needs a grader change the design does not list. The word-ban test includes "run", which ordinary reason sentences contain. There is no check that `maskDeep` leaves the fixed sentences intact, although /mcp and chat mask and POST /actions does not (24-handler.mjs:228).

"Why can't my friend open the link?" is promised more than code can know. `hosted` never returns links (hash only), so "the link I sent" cannot be matched to an item; the design says it never asks, so with several items the brain picks one. hosting-2 does not say ended entries are kept, and a stopped or mistyped link looks the same as one that never existed.

The backstop reply filter is a product-name blocklist inside `sparkieTurn`. Tailscale Funnel is itself a tunnel product, "SSH tunnel" is ordinary wording in this repo (test/eval.mjs), and the list needs upkeep. It would append a ruled-out sentence to a harmless "what is ngrok?" answer.

design.title: Rehearse a saved workflow before it runs, and require one run with the owner present before it may run by itself
design.design:
Outside pieces: none; nothing is installed, so ARM64 does not arise. Three practices were re-read today: Ansible check mode ('just a simulation'; no output for tasks using 'results of prior tasks'), Kubernetes dry-run (every stage runs except the last), Terraform (a saved plan is bound to its state).

Block: Procedure. Data: two fields per entry in saved-workflows.json, `rehearsed {hash, at}` and `ran {hash, at, operation}`; `lastRun` gains `held`. The rest is code. No action, file, timer or page change.

1. /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/src/18-workflows.mjs: `stepsHash(w, inputs)` hashes each step's action and filled-in arguments.
2. Same file: `rehearse(w, inputs, viewer, answers)` walks the steps in order on one fresh inventory. A lookup gets a schema check. A change is previewed through practice-1's no-side-effect path in `runAction` (pause, tested lock, schema, its own rails). Verdicts: goes, nothing to do, would ask, would be refused, checked when reached. It keeps `gone`: what earlier steps stop.
3. /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/src/17-changes.mjs: `railsFor`, `placeModel` and `startModel` take `gone`, so a later start neither lists nor asks about those containers (else 'stop GLM, then start X on Spark 3' is wrongly refused). Checked when reached: an unfilled input; a container an earlier step starts or stops; a restart on a Spark an earlier step changes; a start where an earlier step starts something. Owner-present only: cancel_operation, undo_last_change, test_changes, undo_update.
4. `save_workflow`: checks each step's arguments against its action's schema, refuses `choice`, rehearses when there are no inputs, returns the lines, keeps stamps if steps are unchanged.
5. `run_workflow`: rehearses before `newJob`. Clean: runs as today and stamps `rehearsed`; a completed run the owner started (chat, button, POST /actions) with no answers stamps `ran`. Not clean, owner or agent calling: one `question()` before step 1 carrying the step's own choices, or 'run anyway' for a refusal. Any other caller (the trigger): needs both stamps for this hash, never asks, records `held` and one notice event.
6. /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/src/16-actions.mjs: `sparkieCheck` needs the workflow's name in the owner's words; `what_if` calls `rehearse` and writes nothing.
7. Tests: /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/test/change.test.mjs. /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/docs/architecture.md and docs/contract.md change in the same build.
design.ownerExperience:
Nothing to install, set up or download. From the first sentence:

1. You describe a routine and say "Save that as coding mode and check it first." Sparkie saves it and answers one line per step, for example: "Step 1 would stop sc-qwen3-coder on Spark 3. Step 2 would start GLM-5.3 Flash across Spark 3 and 4 and stop nothing else. Nothing would ask or be refused right now. It cannot run by itself yet: it needs one run you start." A step with a misspelt or unknown argument is refused at save, with its number (today it saves and fails later).

2. "Rehearse coding mode." At any time, the same list from a fresh look at the Sparks. It changes nothing. With Spark 3 and 4 switched off it says so plainly: "Step 2 would be refused right now: Spark 3 is offline."

3. "Run coding mode." It runs as today, after the same check. If a step would ask (a model that answered calls in the last 30 minutes, something you started by hand in the way), that one question comes first, as a button, before anything is touched. If a step would be refused, nothing runs and you are asked whether to run it anyway. Today the run finds out at that step, after the earlier steps already stopped something, and the question has no button.

4. "Can nightly cleanup run by itself yet?" Yes or no with the reason: "Yes: it rehearsed clean at 14:02 and ran with you at 14:05", or "Not yet: it has not run with you since step 2 changed."

5. Once triggers exist (round one): "Run nightly cleanup every night at 2" is accepted only after that. If at 2:00 a step would ask or be refused, nothing is changed and nothing is sent. When you next ask what happened, Sparkie says: "Nightly cleanup did not run at 2:00: step 2 would have asked whether to stop comfy-box."

Your own agents get the same through what_if, run_workflow and workflows at /mcp and POST /console/api/actions/<name>.
design.decidesAndAsks:
Decides by itself, in code and not by the model: to rehearse at save and before every run; which steps can be checked ahead; to drop from a later step's stop list what an earlier step stops; to hold a run nobody is present for when the fresh rehearsal is not clean; to refuse a trigger on steps that have not rehearsed clean and finished one run the owner started; to expire both stamps when a step or a filled-in input changes.

Sparkie's part is only picking the tool. "Rehearse", "check it", "would it work", "can it run by itself" are the lookup (what_if on run_workflow), which always runs because it changes nothing. "Run coding mode" runs at once only when the workflow's name is in the owner's own words; otherwise it is one button reading Run "coding mode". Today a run word alone is enough for run_workflow (the gap noted under R25); this closes it, and the "ran with you" stamp depends on it.

Asks, one question with buttons, before step 1:
- A step's own question, with that step's own choices: a model in use in the last 30 minutes, room only by stopping something Spark Console did not start, a name that matches several models, a repo outside Recipes. A question only the owner may answer stays a button only the owner can press; a typed yes does not press it and an agent is told to ask the owner.
- A step that would be refused right now: "run it anyway, or leave it?" This keeps the owner in charge if the rehearsal is ever wrong about a step.
- After a rehearsal with a step that cannot be checked ahead, it names the step and says the first run with the owner present is what checks it. It does not ask again on every run.

Never asks: a run by itself. It does not start, keeps one line saying why, and waits to be asked.

When confused: a name matching no saved workflow returns the list and Sparkie asks which one; a missing input is asked for by name; a value the owner did not say is not guessed.
guardRails: Wording is fixed: 'nothing would ask or be refused right now', never 'it will work'. Memory after a real load, engine errors and cables are known only when it runs, and every step still goes through runAction with its own plan-again, 8 GB rule, test prompt and put-back.

A rehearsal changes nothing: no claim, no operation, no docker command that changes anything, no button kept, no counted change, no 'change' line in audit.jsonl. what_if writes no file, so 'a read changes nothing' (R11) holds. The test compares each stand-in Spark's container file before and after.

Stamps are written only by save_workflow and run_workflow. `ran` is written only by a completed run the owner started (chat with the workflow's name in the owner's words, a pressed button, or POST /actions, which counts as the owner here as it does everywhere in the console) and only when no question had to be answered. A run by an agent key or by a trigger never stamps.
The stamp names a hash of the steps with their inputs filled in. Change a step, or run with other inputs, and it no longer applies. A trigger must therefore store fixed inputs.

By itself is fail-closed: any caller that is not the owner or an agent key (the trigger, or any way in added later) needs both stamps for this hash, and the rehearsal repeats at run time on a fresh look. Not clean means nothing runs, no button is created and nothing is sent: one line in lastRun and one notice event, bounded by round one's stop after two failures. A paused console holds it too.

A workflow containing undo_update, test_changes, cancel_operation or undo_last_change can never run by itself. The owner decided console updates need their approval, and the other two need an operation or a chat that exists only when someone is there.

Answers to questions live only in the pressed button (in memory, once, 15 minutes, for its asker), never in saved-workflows.json and never in a public schema (R12). Arguments from the saved file are never run as trusted; only the arguments a step's own question produced are. An answer never skips that step's fresh checks when it is reached.
Saved steps cannot carry approval arguments or a choice id (schema check at save), and still cannot save, run or forget workflows or write memory (NOT_A_STEP unchanged).

No timer and no daily dry run: the earlier analysis cut a scheduled dry run of saved workflows as surface for little, and this adds none. No new action, file, page, port, container or download. Sparkie's tool count is unchanged. Nothing touches SSH, Tailscale, the firewall or users; nothing starts on Spark 2.

Text is data: step lines quote container and model names that come from the Sparks, so the result is labelled as data and passes the same masking as other tool results. Whether to run still comes only from the owner's words.

This is not the built-in 'validated on these Sparks' step coming back, which the owner chose to drop. The stamps never block a run the owner asks for; they only decide whether a routine may start with nobody there. The contract's line that saved workflows are 'help, not a gate' (docs/contract.md, about line 1227) is rewritten in the same change, and architecture.md's 'never run steps as trusted' gets its one stated exception.

The edits to railsFor, placeModel and startModel are in the hashed start code, so both start workflows get a new version. Ship them in the same build as practice-1's preview so that happens once, and run the full gate and lock on that exact tree.

Time: the pass shares one inventory look across its steps so it stays inside the 50-second tool limit. If a six-step rehearsal on the real Sparks takes over 30 seconds, share the GPU probes as well (plan() already accepts a probes map).

Why it earns its place for one owner with four Sparks: Spark 3 and 4 are switched on and off by hand, so 'offline', 'in use' and 'something else is running' are the ordinary state a nightly routine meets. Today the run finds out at step 2 or 3, after step 1 has already stopped a model, with nobody there. The cost is about 100 lines in one part and one parameter in another, with no new moving piece.
acceptance: Saving a workflow whose step has an argument its action does not take (a misspelt name, allowStop) or a choice id is refused with the step number; today it saves. The existing saved-workflow test still passes unchanged.

what_if on run_workflow for a two-step workflow (stop the model on spark3, then start another there) lists both steps in order, and step 2's stop list does not include the container step 1 stops. Afterwards every stand-in Spark's ~/.mock/containers file is byte-identical, recent_operations is unchanged, no button exists and audit.jsonl has no new change line.
A workflow that stops a model running across spark3 and spark4 and then starts another model on spark3 rehearses with step 2 as 'goes', not as refused for 'runs across two Sparks'.

With comfy-box (started by hand) holding spark4's memory, a workflow whose step starts a model on spark4 rehearses as 'step 1 would ask' with the question's words. run_workflow from an agent key returns that question before any operation exists, comfy-box is still running, and the note says only the owner can answer. In the owner's chat it is a button, and a typed 'yes' does not press it.

With spark3 in the stand-in fleet's offline file, a workflow whose step 2 needs spark3 starts no operation and names step 2; step 1 did not run (today it would have). Pressing 'run it anyway' runs step 1 and fails at step 2 as today.
A workflow that starts a model and then stops that model's container rehearses step 2 as 'checked when reached', not refused, and the run completes.

After a clean rehearsal and a completed POST /console/api/actions/run_workflow, workflows shows rehearsed and ran with the same hash and 'may run by itself: yes'. Saving again with a changed step shows 'no'; saving again with only the when-text changed keeps 'yes'. A run that needed an answered question completes but does not stamp ran. A run by an agent key completes but does not stamp ran.

A caller that is neither the owner nor an agent key is refused with 'it has not run with you yet' when the stamps are missing. With both stamps and comfy-box in the way, nothing runs, lastRun records held with the reason, no button is created and exactly one notice event is written. Until round one's trigger exists this is tested through the saved view and a direct call in the test; it is tested end to end when the trigger lands.
A workflow containing undo_update or test_changes shows 'may run by itself: no, step N needs you there' however often it has run.

Sparkie on the stand-in fleet: 'run coding mode' runs at once; a message with a start word that does not name the workflow, where the model calls run_workflow, becomes one button reading Run "coding mode" and changes nothing.

On the real brain (test/eval, three runs each): 'rehearse coding mode' and 'can coding mode run by itself yet?' use the lookup and change nothing; 'run coding mode' runs it. If the brain picks wrongly in any run, the tool descriptions are reworded before release.
node test/lock.mjs passes on the exact tree; the tool counts 24 and 37 are unchanged; after install /health shows no workflow untested.

On the real Sparks, the owner's way: save 'coding mode' in chat, ask to rehearse it, run it, then ask whether it can run by itself. The answer is yes with both times, and a six-step rehearsal answers in under 30 seconds. Not run in this analysis: it was read-only, and no test or stand-in fleet was started.
dependsOn: practice-1 (what_if). It does not exist in the code yet. This design needs its preview to go through runAction with a server-set flag, so that: question() returns the question and its choices without keeping a button; start_model, stop_model, restart_model and find_setups return before the claim, the job, the cancelling of other operations and the setups refresh; no change line is audited; nothing is counted by the hourly brake. If practice-1 previews another way, only rehearse() adapts.

Round one's trigger on saved workflows (automation-1), only so the 'by itself' gate has a caller. It must store fixed inputs with the trigger and call run_workflow with its own `via`. The rehearsal, the check before every run and the stamps are useful without it.
A clean full gate and a fresh lock: the tree is already ahead of lock build 4f371d567af6, and this change edits hashed start code, so it should ship in the same build as practice-1.
No dependency on Sparkie's tool cut (no new action), on any owner step, or on any outside software.

Owner's earlier decision to drop the built-in 'validated on these Sparks' step: compatible, because these stamps gate only runs by themselves; worth one sentence to the owner so it is not read as that step returning.

problems: Scope of this attack: read-only. No test, stand-in fleet, SSH or live console was used. File references below are under /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/src/ unless a full path is given. Nothing in the design can lock the owner out, make anything public, or needs another machine, a paid service or new software on ARM64. The problems are complexity, weakened rules and wrong behaviour in the ordinary state (Spark 3 and 4 off).

It is built on practice-1 (what_if), which exists nowhere in the code or docs and has not been attacked. A preview flag through runAction means every change action must return before its side effects, and startModel has several before launch: refreshSetups starts a web look and writes found-setups.json (17-changes.mjs:452), resolveModelName calls Hugging Face for an unknown repo (17-changes.mjs:345, 10-recipes.mjs:86), question() stores a button and calls ctx.onQuestion (17-changes.mjs:49-66), stop_model cancels other operations before its claim (17-changes.mjs:548-549). Reads skip pause, may-change, the intent gate and audit (16-actions.mjs:292), so one missed return is a real change callable by a look-only key at the internet door.

The `gone` parameter edits railsFor, placeModel and startModel, all in START_CODE (18-workflows.mjs:15). Both start workflows get a new version and become needs-validation. Until a validating start, start-on-call is refused with 409 (16-actions.mjs:330-341, via gateway is not in the list; 15-routes.mjs:125) and agent keys get a question; the across workflow needs a real two-Spark start. The design calls this 'happens once'; it is avoidable entirely.

`gone` is an approval argument in disguise. It skips the 'runs across two Sparks' refusal (17-changes.mjs:110-111), the outside-container and routed questions (:112-115) and the in-use question (:443). If it ever reaches a real start through ctx, a model across two Sparks or a hand-started container stops unasked (R8, R12). It is also a simulation of fleet state that the cited practice (Ansible check mode) explicitly does not attempt, and freed memory after a stop on GB10 is not predictable: the real deploy measures it after the stops (07-jobs.mjs:148).

Answering a step's question before step 1 forwards allowStop or allowBusy to a step that may run hours later (each step waits up to 60 minutes, 18-workflows.mjs:197; 12 steps) and runs that step with ctx.trusted, which skips checkInput for the whole step (16-actions.mjs:291). That is the stated exception to 'never run steps as trusted' (architecture.md section 6) and to R12. It also needs `choice` and hidden arguments on run_workflow (schema, PLAN_SKIP, door and fuzz argument tables), so 'no action change' is not true.

The two stamps are a second validation regime, the shape the owner chose to drop (docs/analysis-2026-11-11/README.md, decision 4). They are also flawed as specified: (a) `rehearsed` is redundant, since the rehearsal repeats at fire time; (b) there is one `ran {hash}` per workflow but the hash includes inputs, so an ordinary daytime run with other inputs silently disarms the nightly trigger; (c) a run that answered a question never stamps, so 'coding mode' run by the owner while a model is in use reports 'it has not run with you' straight after the owner ran it.

'Owner present' cannot be read from `via`. An agent through ask_sparkie is via 'sparkie' with only ctx.agent to tell it apart (14-chats.mjs:224-225; 20-mcp.mjs:101). A carry-on turn runs up to 2 hours later as via 'sparkie' on the owner's stored words (14-chats.mjs:137-143, :220-224). POST /actions is any script on the tailnet, and anything that opens api.sock is the owner (architecture.md section 8). The via lists already disagree across the code.

It builds a gate for a caller that does not exist. The trigger (automation-1) is not built and was never attacked, so the 'by itself' half is tested only through a direct call written for the test. As specified it misbehaves in the ordinary state: stop_model on an off Spark is a 404 (17-changes.mjs:536-537), so nightly cleanup is 'held' every night, writes a notice event every night (events must stay rare, R23; the last 10 go to the brain with every message, 19-watcher.mjs:188) and 'stop after two failures' pauses the routine after two nights of the Sparks simply being off.

Unattended runs as designed can stop other models to make room and can download. Both existing unattended callers run with noStops (15-routes.mjs:125; 20-heal.mjs:98); the design's trigger path does not. A start step whose model is no longer on disk downloads it at 2:00 (17-changes.mjs:459-503), against 'no downloads until the owner wants them'. 'In use' lives in memory and only sees calls through the console's address (15-routes.mjs:77-78, :167), so after a console restart it reads clean.

The feature creates its own misfire. 'Dry run coding mode' and 'test run coding mode' contain the start word `run` (16-actions.mjs:104) and the workflow's name. If the 27B brain picks run_workflow instead of the nested what_if(action, args), the design's own name check passes and the workflow runs for real. A title with no distinguishing words ('On', 'It') passes an every() check vacuously. A generic tool nested inside a tool is the hardest tool choice for a 27B model carrying 36 tools.

All-or-nothing changes behaviour for stop-only routines. Today 'stop A on Spark 3, stop B on Spark 4' with Spark 4 off still stops A; with the rehearsal nothing runs unless a 'run anyway' button (another hidden argument) is pressed. The owner's scripts and agents that today get `started` would get a question nobody answers, and nothing is recorded.

Time. The rehearsal runs before newJob: a fresh inventory (du over model folders and curl probes on every Spark, 45 s timeout, 05-library.mjs:80-82) plus one GPU probe per start step (30 s timeout, 05-library.mjs:170) inside a 50 s tool limit (14-chats.mjs:306; 20-mcp.mjs:220). On a slow Spark Sparkie is told 'may still be going' while the run starts later, or the question's button is lost. save_workflow would start doing SSH too.

Upkeep is understated. The rehearsal needs an effects table for every action (what it starts and stops) forever; each new block (workloads, hosting, a smart-plug power step) must declare effects or the rehearsal lies. A future power-on step makes 'Spark 3 is offline' a false refusal. Touch points are runAction, three start functions, four action bodies, question forwarding, stamps, sparkieCheck, what_if and the held event: closer to L than 'about 100 lines'.

Minor leak. The in-use question names which agent or login last called a model (17-changes.mjs:446); what_if would hand that to any look-only key. Held reasons land in `workflows`, which look-only keys read, and notice text reaches the brain's fleet notes unmasked (R7 'Today').

What is right in it and should be kept: checking step arguments at save (today a misspelt argument saves and fails later), finding out before step 1 instead of at step 2 (a failed saved workflow has no put-back for earlier steps), honest fixed wording, and requiring the workflow's name in the owner's words (the R25 gap). These need none of the machinery above.
attack.smallerVersion: One read-only function, `checkSteps(w, inputs)`, in 18-workflows.mjs. No preview flag, no stamps, no start-code edits. One inventory look gives a line per step: arguments pass the action's schema; the Sparks it names are on; a stop or restart finds its container; a start's name matches exactly one model on disk. A step on a Spark an earlier step changes says 'checked when reached'. `save_workflow` runs the schema part and refuses approval arguments. `run_workflow` runs it before `newJob`: a step that cannot run now refuses the run with its number, nothing changed. `workflows {name}` is the rehearsal. Sparkie runs at once only when the workflow's name is in the owner's words. The run-by-itself rule ships with the trigger.
mustHaveGuards: Why it earns its place for one owner: Spark 3 and 4 are off most of the time and a failed saved workflow does not put back its earlier steps, so 'step 2 fails after step 1 stopped a model' is the common failure. About 60 lines in one part, fitting the Procedure block, with no new action, file, timer, page, port or download.

No function listed in any workflow's code() is edited (railsFor, placeModel, startModel, restartChecked, stop_model's body). Test: the five versions in `workflows` are identical before and after, so no validation run is needed and start-on-call keeps working after install.

checkSteps only reads: one inventory, plus existing pure helpers (checkInput, resolveModelName for names on disk or in Recipes, sparkIdOf). It never calls question(), never creates a button, job or claim, writes no file and no audit change line, and never calls Hugging Face: a repo not on disk is reported as 'would download first: checked when reached'. Test: each stand-in Spark's ~/.mock/containers file is byte-identical and recent_operations is unchanged.

Steps are never run as trusted and no answer is stored, forwarded or given ahead. A step that asks still ends the run at that step with the question's words, as today. save_workflow refuses choice, allowStop, allowBusy, confirmOutside, confirmRouted and __validate in step arguments, with the step number. Arguments holding a {placeholder} are checked for their name only at save and in full at run.

The check refuses only on facts that make the real step fail the same way: bad arguments, a named Spark that is off, a container or model that is not there. Everything else is 'goes', 'nothing to do' or 'checked when reached'. The refusal names the step, says nothing was changed and lists the steps that would have gone, so the owner or an agent can ask for those directly. If the check itself throws, the run goes ahead as today and says the check was skipped: a bug in the checker must not stop a workflow.

Wording is fixed in the result, not left to the brain: 'nothing known would stop it right now', never 'it will work'. Lines are fixed templates; container and model names pass the existing schema patterns and the result is labelled as data.

Owners measure about 4 W at the wall when shut down, 22 to 46 W idle (18 to 20 W of that is the 200G link) and about 200 W under load, so the saving is in the shutdown and the plug is what makes power-on possible. Readable without root on ARM64: every thermal zone in /sys/class/thermal (nvidia-smi reads 8 to 15 C lower, and Sparks are widely reported to hard power off near 92 to 96 C leaving no log), NVMe temperature, the kernel journal, boot history and nvidia-smi throttle reasons; NVMe wear needs root (nvme-cli or smartctl, both packaged for ARM64) or possibly UDisks2 (not verified on a Spark), fan speed is not exposed, and the memory has no ECC so there is no error counter. landscapes.landscape: Everything needed for self-hosted research exists on ARM64 today: SearXNG has an official arm64 image (96 MB, checked on Docker Hub 2026-11-11), Local Deep Research 2.0 ships arm64 (835 MB) and takes any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, Crawl4AI 0.9.5 is arm64 (2.9 GB, 4 GB memory), and the `mcp/playwright` image is arm64. The best evidence for a 27B brain is Local Deep Research's community benchmark: Qwen3.6-27B, fully local on one RTX 3090, scored 95.7% on SimpleQA and 77.0% on xbench-DeepSearch (small samples, paid Serper search), level with Alibaba's research-tuned Tongyi DeepResearch 30B (75.0); I found no published research numbers for GLM-5.3 Flash, so the bigger model's edge is unknown until it is measured here. Long reports are weaker ground: hosted systems score about 40 to 49 of 100 on DeepResearch Bench with no 27B entry, and "Cited but Not Verified" (arXiv 2605.06635) found fact-check accuracy of only 39 to 77% even for frontier agents, falling about 42% as tool calls rose from 2 to 150, so a small run with quotes checked by code beats a long crawl. Runs are short: Local Deep Research lists 1 to 5 minutes for a quick answer and 10 to 30 for a report, and at the brain's measured 42 to 63 tokens a second across 2 to 4 requests I estimate 15 to 25 minutes for a 40-source report and about 90 minutes for 150 sources, so "overnight" means unattended, not eight hours. What does not fit: GPT Researcher's Docker image is amd64-only and last pushed in March 2025, and it defaults to Tavily and OpenAI embeddings; LangChain's Open Deep Research was archived in August 2026; Vane (Perplexica) and Local Deep Research are whole apps with their own logins and history; driven browsers fail about one task in three on Qwen3.8-27B (WebArena-Verified 64.8) and VPI-Bench reports browser agents deceived in up to 100% of cases on some platforms. The console has neither search nor a page reader today (contract 6.17 plans both), and the defence that fits it is the map-reduce pattern from "Design Patterns for Securing LLM Agents against Prompt Injections" (arXiv 2506.08837): fetched text only reaches model calls that have no tools, and code decides what is fetched and what is written.

landscapes.landscape: Tailscale Funnel, the door Spark 2 already has, is still beta and serves only the machine's own ts.net name on ports 443, 8443 and 10000 with fixed bandwidth limits; TLS ends on Spark 2 and Tailscale's relays cannot read the traffic, so it is the most private option, and a custom domain is not possible (open requests tailscale/tailscale #11563 and #17913; a CNAME fails because the relay routes by server name), leaving only a redirect from an owned domain to the ts.net link. Cloudflare Tunnel does run on ARM64 Linux (binary, .deb, Docker image) and is free, but it needs a domain on Cloudflare (about $10 to $11 a year for .com, possibly higher since November 2026), a new always-on daemon on Spark 2, ends TLS at Cloudflare, and its free terms bar video and disproportionate large files. A VPS relay (Caddy-L4 or HAProxy passthrough over WireGuard, or Pangolin with its arm64 Newt client) can keep TLS at home but needs a second always-on machine the owner patches for $4 to $6 a month, and dynamic DNS with a home port is free but exposes the home address, needs router and firewall changes by hand and fails behind carrier NAT. What works today with no new server is a static copy on Cloudflare Workers assets (free, 20,000 files of up to 25 MiB, unmetered asset requests, a documented three-call upload), and the product already has that account, a workers.dev subdomain and an outbound-only push (cloud/worker.js, deploy/web-page.sh, pushCloud in 23-http.mjs). One finding from the code: on api.sock the console takes identity from the Tailscale-User-Login header that only Tailscale strips (03-identity.mjs:158-159), so any other front door pointed at that socket would let a visitor claim to be the owner. The honest answer is that the ts.net link is enough for family and friends now; the triggers are a public static site (then a web copy), an address that will be printed or said aloud (then an owned name on that copy), and a live demo for outsiders (only then a tunnel, to a visitors-only socket, for visitor content alone).
